svg.title: Isolated cotangent tests and the proper image of a cycle retract
svg.desc: A symmetric Hessian isolates a smooth cotangent point. The point-cycle inclusion and projection have composite identity after proper pushforward, subject to stated cycle comparisons. The map z to z to the m has m minus one cycles. A proper torus fibre with monodromy two and one has zero cohomology and is not isolated.

g.text: An isolated point-cycle retract survives proper image
Geometric and categorical proofs; general microlocal premises remain explicit
1. A symmetric Hessian isolates the cotangent point [IS.1–IS.5]
U = projection of W; K = W ∩ V*; L = Ann(K)
Choose symmetric B with U × L pairing perfect.
det(t B_U − A) ≠ 0 ⇒ graph(Q) ∩ W = {0}; Q = tB
g(z) = ξ(z) + ½ Q(z,z); dg(y) = ξ; Hess(g) = Q
Zero tangent to graph(dg) ∩ C ⇒ an open, reduced isolated point.
Quasi-finite codifferential fibres transfer isolation; other components are excluded.
2. Push the actual inclusion and projector [IS.6–IS.11]
Cycles(source) = point(V) ⊕ remainder
Proper cycle comparison:
Cycles(Rf_*F) ≃ Rf₀,* Cycles(F)
V
target cycle stalk
V
inclusion
projection
Composite = identity on V. A nonzero V cannot cancel with the remainder.
Application needs detection, cycle t-exactness/completion and proper base change.
3. Exact survival for t = zᵐ, m ≥ 2 [Exercise 3.AC]
C → Cᵐ is the diagonal specialization map.
Φt(Rf_*C[1])₀ = Cᵐ / C(1,…,1), in degree zero
m sectors in every rotated open half-plane; dimension = m − 1
Cotangent equation: m zᵐ⁻¹ η = 0, η ≠ 0
Local fibre ring C[z]₍z₎/(zᵐ⁻¹): isolated support, length m − 1
For m > 2, nilpotent multiplicity remains despite quasi-finiteness.
4. Positive-dimensional proper fibres can cancel [Exercise 3.AD]
Compact complex torus E; rank-one monodromy (2,1)
RΓ(E,L): C → C² → C, v ↦ (v,0), (a,b) ↦ b
h¹(a,b) = a; h²(v) = (0,v); dh + hd = identity
Rf_* i_*L[1] = 0, although every nonzero normal dt occurs at the source.
Fixed cotangent fibre = E, dimension 1: quasi-finiteness fails.
Correspondence dimension 2 > target dimension 1. This is a holomorphic example.
Proofs: Lesson 3, §§3.33–3.35; IS.1–IS.14; solved Exercises 3.AB–3.AD.
Free reading: Arinkin–Gaitsgory–Kazhdan–Raskin–Rozenblyum–Varshavsky,
arXiv:2010.01906v2, Appendix A; Massey, arXiv:math/0006185v2, Theorem 1.1.
All maps are exact indicated maps. General regular-holonomic lower bound remains required.
